items.a: It replaces the reading interface, not the feed engine. FreshRSS continues to fetch and store your subscriptions and articles. FriRSS connects through its Google Reader API.

items.q: Do I need a FreshRSS instance?
items.a: Yes. You need a working FreshRSS instance with API access enabled and an API password set for your FreshRSS account.
FriRSS is free and open source under the MIT license. You provide the hosting. Optional AI providers may charge for their services.
Yes. Official Docker images support amd64 and arm64. Docker Compose and Unraid Community Applications are available too.

items.q: Does it work on my phone?
items.a: Yes. The responsive interface works in a mobile browser, and its PWA can be installed on your home screen. Prepare articles while connected to read them offline. HTTPS is needed for PWA features outside localhost.

items.q: Do I have to use AI?
items.a: No. AI is optional and disabled until an administrator enables it. Reading, organizing and personalizing your feeds work without it.

items.q: Can I choose my AI provider?
items.a: Yes. FriRSS supports Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible providers, including OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama and LM Studio. Provider and model availability depends on your configuration.
